auditor: Claude C (independent, read-only, adversarial, one-shot full-repository final audit)
power_certification_note: Fix4 changed only input guards / validator / hash required-fields / active docs. Bank {-0.04,0,+0.04}, ±0.035 test geometry, residual, probe, DeepSets+HP+5 seeds, primary comparator, block bootstrap, 0.15 CI, seed gate, 300 trials, and legal-input selection are unchanged; learned power 0.984-0.986 (separate from structural 1.000) at the correct block unit stands.
scientific_claim_conclusion: The core proposition (history-conditioned selection beats train/val best-single on unseen NOMINAL test biases, with actual state in-support) is sound, powered, and correctly claim-scoped to SUCCESS. Selection = argmax p_success and the primary endpoint = selected success ONLY; the DeepSets error/time heads are auxiliary multitask signals and do NOT drive selection or the primary, so the experiment does NOT identify a benefit of multidimensional prediction over success-only prediction. The frozen claim_scope does not over-claim this, but the prereg should say it explicitly (FINAL-004).
leakage_conclusion: Clean. Production best-single (select_best_single_confirmatory) reads only {split, session_id, trial_role, theta.grasp_offset_local_y, y.success, planned_episode_id}; secret perturbation invariant; nominal/residual/actual/eff/tau/oracle/test/success-model forbidden and in SECRET_DENYLIST. K0=empty history, K1=1 frozen probe. Simulation-only best_single_legal is not the production entry. No source->component leakage path reaches a deployable model.
manifest_order_conclusion: Deep validator now enforces composition/uniqueness/identity<->PID recompute/referential/per-session/residual-bounds/subseed-recompute/exec-order/planned-subset/frozen-seeds; rejects the bogus 228-duplicate manifest and accepts a valid 228/72 fixture (not over-strict). REMAINING: the candidate/session/block execution ORDER is not uniquely determined by the frozen seed (no canonical subseed->permutation function; validator accepts any bank permutation / unique int) -> FINAL-001; several knowable-now integrity values are format/presence-only -> FINAL-002; one active doc retains stale field names -> FINAL-003.
statistics_conclusion: Correct. Unit = test block (9); per block avg over 2 test nominals then 5 model seeds; gain vs same-block train/val-only best-single; 2000 test-block percentile bootstrap preserving block structure; PRIMARY = CI_lower>=0.15 AND seed gate (>=4/5 point gains>=0.15, none<0); intention-to-analyze keeps all schema-valid outcomes; collision only in secondary sensitivity; VOI/tau secondary, never primary.

issues.summary: No canonical subseed->permutation order-resolution function exists; execution order (candidate order within a session, session order, block order) is not uniquely determined by the frozen seed.
evidence: Exhaustive grep of confirmatory_v4_identity.py / preregistration_v4.py / confirmatory_v4_manifest_integrity.py finds order SUBSEEDS (session_order_subseed, nominal_order_subseed, candidate_order_subseed) but NO function mapping a subseed to a permutation.

validate_fully_resolved_phase_manifest checks resolved_candidate_order only as a length-3 bank permutation (line ~238-243) and block_order_key only as a unique non-bool int; neither is recomputed from a seed; execution_order_index is checked unique/complete but not cross-checked against the order keys; there is no candidate_order_key field (global scan: 0 hits).

manifest_spec §3 states 'resolve block/session/nominal/candidate order from the corresponding order seeds' -> the prereg INTENDS seed-determined order, but the algorithm is undefined (B known_issues §B).
issues.minimal_fix: Freeze one canonical order-resolution function, e.g. resolve_order(subseed, items) -> tuple: build per-item keys ki = subseed(order_seed, item_identity + '|domain=<order>') and return the stable-argsort of items by (ki, item_canonical_index). Apply it to candidate order (per session), session order (per block/split), block order (per split). In validate_fully_resolved_phase_manifest, RE-DERIVE resolved_candidate_order and the block/session order keys from the frozen seeds via this function and reject any mismatch; cross-check execution_order_index against the derived order. ALTERNATIVELY, if execution order is scientifically irrelevant (full reset per trial, block-constant state), drop order randomization: fix a single canonical execution order, remove the order subseeds, and state that order is fixed. Either way the manifest must be uniquely determined by the frozen seeds.
issues.acceptance_test: A frozen resolver exists and is deterministic; validate_fully_resolved_phase_manifest raises ManifestIntegrityError when resolved_candidate_order / block order / session order differ from the seed-recomputed order; two independent constructions from the frozen seeds produce byte-identical order.

Keep commits format-only until the seal step freezes them (document this explicitly). Add a per-field 'source-of-freeze' note (now / generator-commit / train-val-freeze / test-manifest).

issues.summary: The prereg does not explicitly state that the DeepSets error/time heads are auxiliary and that a benefit of multidimensional prediction over success-only prediction is neither claimed nor identified (selection = argmax p_success; primary = selected success only).
evidence: analysis_plan: 'candidate argmax = max p_success'; primary 'select the offset by argmax/tie-break; read selected success'; 'Delta_primary = B2_K1 selected success - best-single success'.

claim_scope frozen wording is success-based and does NOT over-claim multidimensional prediction (so no active over-claim exists) -- but the model is a multitask (success/error/time) network and the paper narrative could imply the multidimensional aspect helps.
issues.minimal_fix: Add one explicit sentence to claim_scope / positioning: 'The error/time regression heads are auxiliary multitask signals; the primary selection and endpoint use p_success only; this experiment does not test or claim that multidimensional (error/time) prediction outperforms success-only prediction.'
issues.acceptance_test: claim_scope / prereg contains an explicit 'error/time heads are auxiliary; multidimensional-prediction superiority not claimed' statement.
